source.title: GSR-BENCH: A Benchmark for Grounded Spatial Reasoning Evaluation via Multimodal LLMs

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream spatial-task performance across multimodal models of different parameter counts, a different task and measure from pretraining-loss scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The results relevant to the claim are the reported downstream accuracy and grounding scores across model sizes. The paper also reports MC option-order sensitivity, depth-augmented prompting, and grounding/localization results by subset; these do not test power-law pretraining loss, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The authors say they scrutinize scaling in this task. They compare spatial-reasoning and grounding accuracy across off-the-shelf multimodal LLMs from 7B to 110B parameters. This is a new downstream setting bearing on V6. It is a weak test: size is confounded with the base LLM, training and visual resolution, and no curve is fitted.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report a positive correlation of overall accuracy with LLM size and visual resolution together, stronger for grounding. They note exceptions they attribute to differences in training, architecture and release date. They see a reasoning plateau at Qwen-1.5-110B, possibly saturation, while grounding keeps rising. Their headline conclusion is that MLLMs beat earlier VLMs by about 26.8 points; they claim no power law.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates multimodal downstream spatial accuracy and grounding rather than held-out language-model loss, compute scaling, or fitted power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that MC option-order bias varies across models and is more detrimental in smaller models; they therefore use template-based generation with CircularEval for the main results.

fits_no_version.finding: Sensitivity to multiple-choice option order is larger in smaller models; LLaVA-NeXT-Yi-34B and LLaMA-3-LLaVA-NeXT-8B are more robust (Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness to multiple-choice option-order bias increases with model size in MLLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: A linear regression of reasoning accuracy on grounding accuracy (Subset A subjects) gives β=6.025, p=0.007.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grounding ability predicts spatial reasoning accuracy across MLLMs.

record.code_released: The text says code and data will be publicly available; no URL or release confirmation is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2024 Workshop on Compositional Learning: Perspectives, Methods, and Paths Forward
record.problems: The authors note that the benchmark is small-scale, uses pseudo-labels without human annotation, and has limited spatial prepositions. Model size is confounded with architecture, training/fine-tuning, release date, and visual resolution. No uncertainty estimates or scaling-curve fits are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 subset-level accuracies and Table 2 per-subset localization results are not separately cataloged; the overall measures relevant to cross-size comparison are retained. MC option-order sensitivity and depth-augmented prompting do not measure the claim versions tested.

untested.parts: Whether downstream performance is predictable (a fitted curve or prediction from pretraining loss). Also controlled scaling within a single training recipe.
No power-law fits on multimodal loss.

missing.what: Subset-level reversals with size. Subset B accuracy falls from 7B to 13B in both families: LLaVA-1.5 31.9→28.2, NeXT-Vicuna 26.2→20.1.
Grounding of small objects (Subset A subject) rises with size, 9.7→29.4, but stays low for all models.
InternVL-1.5 grounding results are omitted because of noisy outputs.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is cross-model and confounded: size, base LLM, visual resolution and instruction tuning all vary, with no uncertainty estimates and no fitted curve. Only the two within-family 7B/13B pairs are cleanish size comparisons. The 41.7% random-chance baseline in the rows is the wrong baseline for scaling; states were reassigned using pairwise size comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law forms in other modalities or training regimes; the study evaluates multimodal task accuracy but does not fit or test scaling laws.
The study evaluates spatial reasoning and grounding accuracy across models, but does not test prediction from pretraining loss or fit a downstream scaling curve.
Effects of fit choices on scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits, and departures from power-law loss curves.

relationships.condition: Within-family 7B→13B pairs (LLaVA-1.5-Vicuna, LLaVA-NeXT-Vicuna), for both reasoning and grounding
relationships.reason: The larger variant is higher in every pair: reasoning 61.3→72.3 and 68.1→75.3 (r1, r2, r4, r5); grounding 44.62→56.74 and 68.13→75.93 (r10, r11, r12, r14).
relationships.display_finding: Reasoning scores increased from 61.3 to 72.3 and 68.1 to 75.3, while grounding increased from 44.62 to 56.74 and 68.13 to 75.93.

relationships.condition: Spatial reasoning accuracy across LLaVA-NeXT models from 8B to 110B with different base LLMs
relationships.reason: Reasoning accuracy plateaus: 86.1 at 8B, 87.2 at 34B, 85.4 at 110B (r6, r7, r8). Same-size 7B models also differ by about 10 points (r3 vs r4).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy was 86.1 at 8B, 87.2 at 34B, and 85.4 at 110B, while same-size 7B models differed by about 10 points.

relationships.condition: Grounding G-score across LLaVA-NeXT models from 8B to 110B
relationships.reason: Grounding keeps rising, 77.92→79.01→81.61 (r15, r16, r17), though the gains are small and the base LLMs differ.
relationships.display_finding: Grounding G-scores increased from 77.92 to 79.01 to 81.61, although gains were small and the underlying language models differed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Same-named model families with reported parameter variants
reader_labels.reason: The larger variants have higher total spatial accuracy in the LLaVA-1.5-Vicuna pair and LLaVA-NeXT-Vicuna pair (r1, r2, r4, r5); grounding scores also rise in these pairs (r10, r11, r12, r14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the tested architectures and model sizes on GSR-Bench
reader_labels.reason: The authors report exceptions and a plateau in reasoning accuracy; the models differ in architecture, training/fine-tuning, release date, and visual resolution, and the study does not fit or validate a predictive scaling curve (r3, r6, r7, r8, r9, r13, r15, r16, r17).
